name: John P. Belding
bio: John P. Belding, ex-sheriff of Lawrence County and a capital commissioner, traveled through Medora between Deadwood and the East in 1884, once arriving only thirty-six hours from Deadwood. In early 1885 he was in Bismarck, where he was elected president, or speaker, of the "third house."

Elected president of the 'third house' at Bismarck

mentions: John Belding, ex-sheriff of Lawrence county and one of the capital commissioners passed through here Tuesday, on his way east. He was only thirty-six hours from Deadwood.

Pat. Smith of Bismarck and John Belding of Deadwood, got off last night to take our stage line to the Hills, having been informed that it was running. As it was, the cayuse-buckboard line from Miles City recei…
…. A. McCall, Hon. H. A. Sprague, Hon. H. M. Gregg, J. A. Bishop, Kane Holland, Hon. G. T. Bennett and John P. Belding, sheriff of Lawrence county.
Judge Bennett, of Deadwood, went down on Monday's coach. Ex-Sheriff Belding, who came up with him, still lingers in Bismarck, where he has been unanimously elected president of the third house.
Ex-sheriff Belding, of Deadwood, and speaker of the third house at Bismarck, went home on last Friday's coach.
